entity-newcomer-after-settlescene-entity-transitions0.75 of 0.75 (major)passThe kit sequences a newcomer&#39;s entry after the continuing entities&#39; layout motion by timing, and every entity the sample introduces goes through that same path. In src/presentation-kit/constants.ts, LAYOUT_T has duration 0.45 and ENTER_DELAY is 0.48. ENTER_T is { duration: 0.24, delay: 0.48 }. ENTITY_T is { layout: LAYOUT_T, opacity: ENTER_T }, so the delay sits only on the opacity key and the layout key has no delay. Box (src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx) is a motion.div with layout, layoutId, initial opacity 0, animate opacity 1 and transition={ENTITY_T}. Arrow (src/presentation-kit/nodes/Arrow.tsx) is a motion.svg with the same props. A persisting entity already has opacity 1, so it only runs the undelayed 0.45s layout transition. A newcomer mounts at opacity 0 and stays invisible until 0.48s, which is after the 0.45s layout settles. The only browser-driving tests are in tests/integration.test.mjs: INT-001, INT-002, E2E-001 and E2E-002. They reach a browser only by spawning `npm run verify` or `npm run inspect` through command(). command() has no sleep. Its setTimeout is a SIGKILL timeout guard, and every assertion runs after the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; event. In verify, the render loop at scripts/verify.mjs:36-46 calls settleStep(page, index) before reading the marker, title and caption from the DOM and before printing PASS render step. If the step never advances, waitForFunction throws, as E2E-002&#39;s &#39;transition&#39; fault shows. Judges A and B are correct, and their reasons decide the criterion: the tests contain no fixed sleeps, and the scripts they run wait for state through waitForFunction. Judge C correctly notes that settleStep also calls page.waitForTimeout(settle), and that INT-002 checks elapsedBeforeCapture &gt;= 900. That sleep runs only after the polling wait has already confirmed the step index. It is an extra animation-settle delay before the screenshot, not a replacement for waiting on state, and no step is asserted on the strength of that sleep alone. Human review
#QuestionRatingRationale
1Across the full presentation, how good do the titles, captions, labels, and other content text look and read? Judge whether important content text is visibly present, typography, sizing, weight, spacing, line breaks, contrast, legibility, visual hierarchy, and whether the wording is clear, intentional, and audience-ready rather than sounding like an internal annotation. Do not judge navigation controls or presentation chrome here, and do not judge the placement or styling of non-text elements.4 / 5typography bit small
2How well designed are the individual scene elements, such as boxes, arrows, icons, illustrations, and diagram nodes? Judge their shapes, proportions, fills, borders, detail, consistency, and overall craft. Do not judge their text, placement, movement, or navigation chrome here.4 / 5—
3At a normal wide viewport, how well are the text and visual elements arranged relative to one another? Judge alignment, spacing, grouping, balance, focal points, use of space, and whether anything feels crowded, disconnected, clipped, or unintentionally overlapping. Judge viewport adaptation separately under responsive visual quality.5 / 5—
4As you advance through the presentation, how well do the animations and scene changes work? Judge smoothness, pacing, meaningful entrances and exits, continuity of persistent elements, and whether each step visibly evolves the existing scene instead of feeling like an unrelated replacement.5 / 5—
5Taken as a whole, how strong is the presentation’s visual identity? Judge its color palette, background treatment, stylistic consistency, brand character, polish, memorability, and whether it feels intentionally designed and finished. Judge the craft of individual scene elements separately.4 / 5—
6How clear, discoverable, and visually integrated are the presentation controls and chrome? Judge progress indicators, previous/next controls, table of contents, mode switching, and attribution. Focus on their appearance and ease of understanding, not whether every input method technically works or how content captions are styled.5 / 5—
7Compare the presentation at wide and narrow viewport sizes. How well does its hierarchy and composition adapt? Judge scaling, density, readability, control accessibility, clipping, overlap, and whether the narrow version still feels intentionally composed. Judge baseline wide-screen composition separately.4 / 5—

The parts that pass: the title prop is passed from Talk to Presentation to Header and rendered in data-presentation-document-title, every entities member is consumed as a key and id in Scene.tsx, and the demo-specific logic stays inside its presentation folder. (1) Every readiness wait is bounded. withBrowser polls in a loop of at most 100 iterations with a 50ms back-off, aborts at once if the spawned preview exits or fails to launch, and then throws &#39;preview readiness timeout&#39;. The page-level wait in readStepCount has a 5000ms timeout, and settleStep&#39;s waitForFunction has a 3000ms timeout. (2) verify() and inspect() both `await build(root)` before calling withBrowser. build() resolves only when the `npm run build` child exits with code 0, so the preview starts only after the build has completed. (3) Readiness comes from an HTTP fetch of the 127.0.0.1 URL, not from parsing the server&#39;s printed ready URL. serverOutput is used only in error messages, so the ANSI and split-chunk clause does not apply. Judge C failed this because each `await fetch(url)` has no abort signal. That does not show any clause unmet. The loop&#39;s iteration cap, its early exit when the child exits, and the final timeout error bound the readiness wait. The cited source shows no case where a single fetch hangs against the script&#39;s own vite preview, and the criterion does not ask for a per-request abort signal. (1) Every readiness wait is bounded. withBrowser polls in a loop of at most 100 iterations with a 50ms back-off, aborts at once if the spawned preview exits or fails to launch, and then throws &#39;preview readiness timeout&#39;. The page-level wait in readStepCount has a 5000ms timeout, and settleStep&#39;s waitForFunction has a 3000ms timeout. (2) verify() and inspect() both `await build(root)` before calling withBrowser. build() resolves only when the `npm run build` child exits with code 0, so the preview starts only after the build has completed. (3) Readiness comes from an HTTP fetch of the 127.0.0.1 URL, not from parsing the server&#39;s printed ready URL. serverOutput is used only in error messages, so the ANSI and split-chunk clause does not apply. Judge C failed this because each `await fetch(url)` has no abort signal. That does not show any clause unmet. The loop&#39;s iteration cap, its early exit when the child exits, and the final timeout error bound the readiness wait. The cited source shows no case where a single fetch hangs against the script&#39;s own vite preview, and the criterion does not ask for a per-request abort signal. Here, every step check waits on state first. vitest.config.ts runs tests/**/*.test.{ts,tsx} under jsdom, so kit.test.tsx, sample.test.tsx, scripts.test.ts and style.test.ts do not drive a browser. The only browser-driving tests are in tests/integration.test.mjs: INT-001, INT-002, E2E-001 and E2E-002. They reach a browser only by spawning `npm run verify` or `npm run inspect` through command(). command() has no sleep. Its setTimeout is a SIGKILL timeout guard, and every assertion runs after the child&#39;s &#39;exit&#39; event. In verify, the render loop at scripts/verify.mjs:36-46 calls settleStep(page, index) before reading the marker, title and caption from the DOM and before printing PASS render step. Inspect, at scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:16-27, also calls settleStep before running diagnostics and taking the screenshot. settleStep (scripts/browser-runtime.mjs:74-77) first runs page.waitForFunction, which polls until data-step-index equals the target index, with a 3000 ms timeout. readStepCount (lines 68-73) uses an auto-waiting locator.waitFor before it reads the count, so the read is not treated as if it had waited. If the step never advances, waitForFunction throws, as E2E-002&#39;s &#39;transition&#39; fault shows. Judges A and B are correct, and their reasons decide the criterion: the tests contain no fixed sleeps, and the scripts they run wait for state through waitForFunction. Judge C correctly notes that settleStep also calls page.waitForTimeout(settle), and that INT-002 checks elapsedBeforeCapture &gt;= 900. That sleep runs only after the polling wait has already confirmed the step index. It is an extra animation-settle delay before the screenshot, not a replacement for waiting on state, and no step is asserted on the strength of that sleep alone. The guidance also says longer fixed settle delays are neither credited nor scored. bootstrap template copy. (1) Timeouts: the readiness loop in withBrowser runs at most 100 times with a 50ms back-off. It stops early if the child exits or fails to launch, and otherwise throws &#39;preview readiness timeout&#39;. The page-level waits are also bounded: readStepCount waits up to 5000ms and settleStep&#39;s waitForFunction up to 3000ms. AT-003 additionally expects important content to remain readable at a narrow viewport. At 390 × 844, the scene fits at scale 0.389 and its card labels become very small. What minimum readable size or behavior should govern narrow viewports?"},{"line":769,"text":""},{"line":770,"text":"**Observed evidence:** `acceptance-screenshots/step-05-dense-narrow-052e4093.png`, `step-01-first-narrow-052e4093.png`, and `step-09-last-narrow-052e4093.png`; live DOM reports `data-scale=\"0.3886363636363636\"` while retaining `880px × 380px` canvas geometry."},{"line":771,"text":""},{"line":772,"text":"**Options and consequences:** Keep strict uniform scaling and accept that detailed labels are hard to read on narrow phones; allow a minimum scale and overflow/zoom, which may no longer fit the entire scene; or define a separate narrow presentation treatment, which risks changing the fixed canvas's internal composition. I have recorded a usability defect against the test-plan readability expectation; the product/design threshold and acceptable narrow-view behavior remain for human review."},{"line":773,"text":""},{"line":774,"text":"## Acceptance round 0, F-002: header overlap warnings that are not visually present"},{"line":775,"text":""},{"line":776,"text":"**Question:** The tester reproduced two overlap warnings on every sample step at 1440 × 900: the mode toggle against the marker and against the document title. The screenshots show clear separation. Is this a defect?"},{"line":777,"text":""},{"line":778,"text":"**Requirement:**"},{"line":779,"text":"- `specs/presentation-verification/spec.md`, \"Suspicious overlap is reported\": warn when \"visible text or presentation chrome overlaps another visible text/chrome element\"."},{"line":780,"text":"- Ruling \"Overlap diagnostics\" above made chrome-element rectangles a party to the check."},{"line":781,"text":""},{"line":782,"text":"**Ruling:** It is a defect in my implementation of that ruling, not a spec question. I collected the border box of every chrome hook. The marker and document title are block-level elements whose boxes span the whole header (x=24…1416) although their glyphs are left-aligned, so the box intersected the right-aligned toggle. Fix: chrome that is not a `button` or `a` and contains visible text no longer contributes a box, because its glyph rectangles are already collected. Interactive controls keep their padded box, and text-less chrome such as an icon-only brand keeps its box. The earlier ruling still holds for the cases it was written for."},{"line":783,"text":""},{"line":784,"text":"**Rationale:** An advisory warning that fires on every step of the committed sample would train authors to ignore the list, and the skill's warning-review loop would chase non-collisions. The spec wording (\"visible text/chrome element\") is satisfied by the visible glyphs of text chrome."},{"line":785,"text":""},{"line":786,"text":"**Evidence:**"},{"line":787,"text":"- Regression test \"I-45 block-level text chrome uses glyph bounds while interactive chrome keeps its padded box\" in `tests/scripts.test.ts`, run with `evidence/F-002-unit.log` (10 of 10 pass)."},{"line":788,"text":"- The same test fails against the pre-fix `scripts/diagnostics.mjs`: `evidence/F-002-unit-prefix.log` shows the marker and title boxes collected."},{"line":789,"text":"- `evidence/F-002-lint.log` and `evidence/F-002-types.log` are clean."},{"line":790,"text":"- The root script and the bootstrap template copy are byte-identical."},{"line":791,"text":""},{"line":792,"text":"**Integration regression recommendation:** INT-002 should gain a header-like fixture (a full-width block marker with a right-aligned button) that asserts no overlap warning in real browser geometry. I did not add it because integration and end-to-end suites were not to be run in this step, and an unrun browser test could break the next round. It is a meaningful addition for a later pass."},{"line":793,"text":""},{"line":794,"text":"**Pending from the user:** None."},{"line":795,"text":""},{"line":796,"text":"## Acceptance round 0, F-001: sample diagram text is 5 to 7 CSS pixels at a 390-pixel viewport"},{"line":797,"text":""},{"line":798,"text":"**Question:** At 390 × 844 the 880 × 380 canvas scales to about 0.389, so the card titles and labels render at roughly 5 to 7 CSS pixels. AT-003 expects \"important content remains readable ... at both viewport widths\". Should this be fixed?"},{"line":799,"text":""},{"line":800,"text":"**Requirement:**"},{"line":801,"text":"- `specs/evolving-scene-presentations/spec.md`, \"Fixed-canvas fit scaling\": the diagram is \"scaled uniformly to fit the available viewport, so the composition does not reflow\". \"The default design canvas SHALL be 880 × 380, with per-mode fit geometry for the browse and present layouts.\""},{"line":802,"text":"- Same file, \"Uniform scaling on resize\": scaling is uniform with no reflow of the internal composition."},{"line":803,"text":"- `design.md` Stage: scale is constant within a mode so `layoutId` morphs stay clean."},{"line":804,"text":"- `test-plan.md` AT-003 asks for readable content and a narrow-viewport pass."},{"line":805,"text":"- The sample's typography and geometry are deferred to design, and the sample must keep entities stationary across beats."},{"line":806,"text":""},{"line":807,"text":"**Ruling:** No code change, and I am escalating. The scale is determined by the approved fixed canvas: (390 − 2 × 24) / 880 = 0.389. Reaching comfortable text at that width needs one of:"},{"line":808,"text":"1. A different canvas or a narrow-viewport layout, which departs from the approved \"uniform scaling, no reflow\" requirement and the \"880 × 380 default\" requirement."},{"line":809,"text":"2. A per-viewport sample layout, which breaks the \"entities are never rearranged\" sample requirement unless a second composition is authored."},{"line":810,"text":"3. Larger sample typography on the existing geometry. That is within the presentation's own design latitude, but the cards are 132 × 86 and the smallest labels are already 9 to 12 px. Even 16 px design text renders at about 6 px, so it cannot meet a comfortable reading size, and I cannot confirm in this step that larger text would fit the cards without new collisions."},{"line":811,"text":""},{"line":812,"text":"I did not change the margin or typography. The change would be marginal (the margin saves a few percent of scale) and cannot reach comfortable readability, and it adds unverified risk."},{"line":813,"text":""},{"line":814,"text":"**Rationale:** The observation is correct, but it follows from approved requirements. The narrow-view expectation in AT-003 and the fixed-canvas requirement can only both hold if \"readable\" is read as \"legible when zoomed or as part of a scaled whole\", which is a product decision."},{"line":815,"text":""},{"line":816,"text":"**Pending from the user (decision needed):** Choose one:"},{"line":817,"text":"- (a) Accept the uniform-scale behavior at phone widths as intended. AT-003's narrow-view clause is then interpreted as \"fits without reflow or collision\"."},{"line":818,"text":"- (b) Approve a narrow-viewport mechanism (a second per-mode canvas, a minimum scale with scrolling, or an authored narrow composition). That changes the fixed-canvas and no-reflow requirements and needs a spec update."},{"line":819,"text":"- (c) Approve modest typography increases in the sample only, accepting that this will not reach comfortable readability at 390 px."},{"line":820,"text":""},{"line":821,"text":"Until the user decides, the implementation stays as is."},{"line":822,"text":""}],"label":"[artifact candidate-0c74b4fc9e9bc4f7 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":823,"end_line":859,"lines":[{"line":823,"text":"## Acceptance round 1, F-003: styled text-bearing chrome was dropped from overlap checks"},{"line":824,"text":""},{"line":825,"text":"**Question:** The round 0 fix for F-002 stopped collecting the box of non-interactive chrome whenever it contained visible text. The tester showed that a host brand styled as a bordered, semi-transparent 240 × 80 px box can sit on a scene label (\"you\") and produce no warning, because only its \"HOST BRAND\" glyphs were compared. Is this a defect?"},{"line":826,"text":""},{"line":827,"text":"**Requirement:**"},{"line":828,"text":"- `specs/presentation-verification/spec.md`, \"Suspicious overlap is reported\": warn when \"visible text or presentation chrome overlaps another visible text/chrome element\"."},{"line":829,"text":"- My ruling \"Overlap diagnostics\" above made chrome elements a party to the check."},{"line":830,"text":""},{"line":831,"text":"**Ruling:** It is a defect. My F-002 fix was too broad. A box is visible chrome only when it is decorated, so the rule is now:"},{"line":832,"text":"- Non-interactive text chrome contributes its box if its computed style has a non-transparent background, a border with non-zero width and a style other than none, or a box shadow. Otherwise it contributes only its glyph rectangles, which is the F-002 case (an unstyled block-level marker or title spanning the header)."},{"line":833,"text":"- Buttons and links always contribute their box, as before."},{"line":834,"text":"- Text-less chrome keeps its box, as before."},{"line":835,"text":"- The sample's marker, title and caption carry no decoration, so the F-002 result is preserved."},{"line":836,"text":""},{"line":837,"text":"**Rationale:** Padding on an undecorated element is invisible, so glyph bounds are its visible extent. A visible background, border or shadow makes the whole rectangle part of what the viewer sees. This keeps the false positive from F-002 away and restores the collision the spec asks for."},{"line":838,"text":""},{"line":839,"text":"**Evidence:**"},{"line":840,"text":"- `tests/scripts.test.ts`, \"I-45 decorated text chrome keeps its visible box so a styled brand colliding with scene text warns\". It covers a background, a border, and a fully transparent background (no box)."},{"line":841,"text":"- `evidence/F-003-unit.log` shows 11 of 11 passing. `evidence/F-003-unit-prefix.log` shows the new case failing against the previous script."},{"line":842,"text":"- `evidence/F-003-lint.log` and `evidence/F-003-types.log` are clean."},{"line":843,"text":"- The root script and the bootstrap template copy are byte-identical."},{"line":844,"text":""},{"line":845,"text":"**Integration regression recommendation:** INT-002 should add a styled-brand fixture whose box overlaps scene text and a plain full-width marker next to a right-aligned button, asserting a warning for the first and none for the second in real browser geometry. Not added now because integration suites are not run in this step."},{"line":846,"text":""},{"line":847,"text":"**Pending from the user:** None."},{"line":848,"text":""},{"line":849,"text":"## Acceptance round 1, F-001: carried over, still awaiting the user"},{"line":850,"text":""},{"line":851,"text":"**Question:** The tester reproduced the 5 to 7 px diagram text at 390 × 844 again (scale 0.389)."},{"line":852,"text":""},{"line":853,"text":"**Requirement:** Unchanged from the \"Acceptance round 0, F-001\" entry above: fixed 880 × 380 canvas, uniform scaling, no internal reflow, and AT-003's narrow-view readability expectation."},{"line":854,"text":""},{"line":855,"text":"**Ruling:** No code change this round. The behavior still follows from the approved fixed-canvas requirement, and the choice between (a) accepting it, (b) approving a narrow-viewport mechanism with a spec update, or (c) modest sample typography increases is the user's decision, as recorded in the round 0 entry and in \"Narrow viewport readability threshold\"."},{"line":856,"text":""},{"line":857,"text":"**Rationale:** Any fix changes the approved scaling or sample composition requirements. Nothing new was learned that changes that assessment."},{"line":858,"text":""},{"line":859,"text":"**Pending from the user (decision needed):** Choose (a), (b) or (c) as described in the round 0 F-001 entry."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-0c74b4fc9e9bc4f7 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":934,"end_line":967,"lines":[{"line":934,"text":"## F-001 — Diagram labels are too small at the narrow viewport (reproduced in round 1)"},{"line":935,"text":""},{"line":936,"text":"- **Affected behavior:** Responsive composition of the reference presentation."},{"line":937,"text":"- **Expected:** AT-003 expects important scene content to remain readable at a narrow viewport while the 880 × 380 design canvas scales uniformly."},{"line":938,"text":"- **Observed:** At 390 × 844 the canvas has `data-scale=\"0.3886363636363636\"`; card titles and labels are reduced to roughly 5–7 CSS pixels and are difficult to read. This does not change an approved requirement. I-28 and I-29 require the skill to instruct the agent to review the output visually. They do not require the implementor to do that review for this repository."},{"line":670,"text":""},{"line":671,"text":"**Rationale:**"},{"line":672,"text":"- It follows the plain wording of the checklist, `implement-change` and the current instruction, and it weakens none of them."},{"line":673,"text":"- The test plan puts browser-based visual quality and skill behavior under agent acceptance (AT-003 and AT-004), a separate stage, and requires INT-002 and E2E-001/E2E-002 for the deterministic parts."},{"line":674,"text":"- The prohibition on prompt-text tests exists because text matching proves nothing about how an agent behaves, so reading is the appropriate check."},{"line":675,"text":""},{"line":676,"text":"**Pending from the user:**"},{"line":677,"text":"- No decision is needed to proceed."},{"line":678,"text":"- The completion report must say plainly that the implementor did no AXI inspection and no screenshot review, and that this was left to the independent tester under the current instruction. CLAUDE.md's \"inspect representative steps with AXI and the project-local screenshot helper\" requirement is therefore unmet by the implementor on purpose."},{"line":679,"text":"- It must also name any test tiers left unrun, as `implement-change` requires."},{"line":680,"text":"- If the user wants the CLAUDE.md inspection requirement to apply after all, they need to say so. Until then this ruling stands."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-0c74b4fc9e9bc4f7 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":704,"end_line":706,"lines":[{"line":704,"text":"**Rationale:** The literal wording lists chrome as an overlapping party. A button's padded box is part of that chrome and occupies the space viewers see. The shipped kit's own controls carry text, so glyph rectangles cover them partly, but the host-supplied attribution or brand and any restyled icon-only control show the gap. The alternative reading (glyph-only) is a plausible narrower interpretation, but it cannot be derived from the text. Emitting extra advisory warnings does not violate that reading, since the helper never fails a run on warnings (I-47)."},{"line":705,"text":""},{"line":706,"text":"**Pending from the user:** None blocking. Escalated for awareness only: if the user wants glyph-only detection as the deliberate scope, they must say so, because that would narrow the spec's \"text or presentation chrome\" wording."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-0c74b4fc9e9bc4f7 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":728,"end_line":730,"lines":[{"line":728,"text":"- Warnings are advisory, so the stricter reading does not conflict with the other one."},{"line":729,"text":""},{"line":730,"text":"**Pending from the user:** None blocking. Escalated for awareness: the \"match all inactive controls\" reading would yield fewer warnings. The user should override only if they want that."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-0c74b4fc9e9bc4f7 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":807,"end_line":821,"lines":[{"line":807,"text":"**Ruling:** No code change, and I am escalating. The scale is determined by the approved fixed canvas: (390 − 2 × 24) / 880 = 0.389. Reaching comfortable text at that width needs one of:"},{"line":808,"text":"1. A different canvas or a narrow-viewport layout, which departs from the approved \"uniform scaling, no reflow\" requirement and the \"880 × 380 default\" requirement."},{"line":809,"text":"2. A per-viewport sample layout, which breaks the \"entities are never rearranged\" sample requirement unless a second composition is authored."},{"line":810,"text":"3. Larger sample typography on the existing geometry. That is within the presentation's own design latitude, but the cards are 132 × 86 and the smallest labels are already 9 to 12 px. Even 16 px design text renders at about 6 px, so it cannot meet a comfortable reading size, and I cannot confirm in this step that larger text would fit the cards without new collisions."},{"line":811,"text":""},{"line":812,"text":"I did not change the margin or typography. The change would be marginal (the margin saves a few percent of scale) and cannot reach comfortable readability, and it adds unverified risk."},{"line":813,"text":""},{"line":814,"text":"**Rationale:** The observation is correct, but it follows from approved requirements. The narrow-view expectation in AT-003 and the fixed-canvas requirement can only both hold if \"readable\" is read as \"legible when zoomed or as part of a scaled whole\", which is a product decision."},{"line":815,"text":""},{"line":816,"text":"**Pending from the user (decision needed):** Choose one:"},{"line":817,"text":"- (a) Accept the uniform-scale behavior at phone widths as intended. AT-003's narrow-view clause is then interpreted as \"fits without reflow or collision\"."},{"line":818,"text":"- (b) Approve a narrow-viewport mechanism (a second per-mode canvas, a minimum scale with scrolling, or an authored narrow composition). That changes the fixed-canvas and no-reflow requirements and needs a spec update."},{"line":819,"text":"- (c) Approve modest typography increases in the sample only, accepting that this will not reach comfortable readability at 390 px."},{"line":820,"text":""},{"line":821,"text":"Until the user decides, the implementation stays as is."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-0c74b4fc9e9bc4f7 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":849,"end_line":859,"lines":[{"line":849,"text":"## Acceptance round 1, F-001: carried over, still awaiting the user"},{"line":850,"text":""},{"line":851,"text":"**Question:** The tester reproduced the 5 to 7 px diagram text at 390 × 844 again (scale 0.389)."},{"line":852,"text":""},{"line":853,"text":"**Requirement:** Unchanged from the \"Acceptance round 0, F-001\" entry above: fixed 880 × 380 canvas, uniform scaling, no internal reflow, and AT-003's narrow-view readability expectation."},{"line":854,"text":""},{"line":855,"text":"**Ruling:** No code change this round. The behavior still follows from the approved fixed-canvas requirement, and the choice between (a) accepting it, (b) approving a narrow-viewport mechanism with a spec update, or (c) modest sample typography increases is the user's decision, as recorded in the round 0 entry and in \"Narrow viewport readability threshold\"."},{"line":856,"text":""},{"line":857,"text":"**Rationale:** Any fix changes the approved scaling or sample composition requirements. The ledger records that temporal motion is optional under the approved requirement; unchanged by this pass."},{"line":910,"text":"- AT-001/AT-002/AT-004 limitations: no independent target-agent workflow was available in this acceptance setup, so those skill-led journeys have no independent runtime evidence. Human warning review remains necessary; the current round exercised decorated and transparent backgrounds/borders only."},{"line":919,"text":"- Notable — Navigation and fit geometry: 40px horizontal swipe threshold, ToC at 1100px, fixed per-mode chrome reserve, and unrestricted downscaling can affect swipe response, ToC availability, and small-screen legibility."},{"line":920,"text":"- Notable — Group identity and primitive entry behavior: recreating scene components or wrapping continuing entities with entry wrappers may reset state or cause unwanted fades; independent browser motion acceptance should review these cases."},{"line":921,"text":"- Notable — Scaffold and reference verification modes: the neutral two-step bootstrap and canonical nine-step verification route differ; a newly registered scaffold route may be omitted from the default gate unless the skill explicitly verifies it."},{"line":922,"text":"- Notable — Registry fallback/configured verification routes: unknown paths display Landing, which may conceal a mistyped route; root verification checks the canonical route even when another route is supplied."},{"line":923,"text":"- Notable — Browser failure phases and cleanup: errors scheduled after the observation interval may escape detection, and transition timeouts may obscure the original browser exception."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-1754e2bee5a73ca0 (final-handoff)]"}]},"results":[{"id":"assumption-repository-facts-distinguished","verdict":"pass","rationale":"The record classifies every requirement violation it reproduced as a defect. The user controls how much to specify; the skill SHALL NOT assume details the user can still provide, but SHALL allow the user to proceed with partial detail and iterate. The skill MAY, at its discretion, draw ASCII mockups to represent key or complex steps when doing so helps confirm the intended visual layout.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Prompt is missing details\\n- **WHEN** the skill is invoked with a prompt that omits the topic, visual style, or per-step descriptions\\n- **THEN** the skill asks for the missing information one question at a time rather than assuming it\\n\\n#### Scenario: User proceeds with partial detail\\n- **WHEN** the user chooses to build after providing only some details\\n- **THEN** the skill generates a presentation from what was captured without blocking on a hard completeness gate\\n\\n#### Scenario: Prompt already complete\\n- **WHEN** the prompt already contains the topic, style, and all step details\\n- **THEN** the skill may proceed to build without further questions\\n\\n#### Scenario: ASCII mockup for a complex step\\n- **WHEN** a step's visual layout is key or complex\\n- **THEN** the skill may present an ASCII mockup of that step to the user to confirm the layout before building, without doing so for every step\\n\\n### Requirement: Self-bootstrapping scaffold\\nBefore creating or modifying a presentation, the skill SHALL ensure the project provides the infrastructure a generated presentation depends on, SHALL resolve where that infrastructure belongs, and SHALL scaffold whatever is missing — including installing the dependencies the infrastructure requires. The required infrastructure is three contract anchors:\\n\\n1. **Build setup** — a Vite + React + TypeScript app with a working `npm run build`.\\n2. **Scene kit** — the reusable, presentation-agnostic engine: the `Step`/`Scene` step contract, the stage/host that mounts the active step and runs entity morphs, the present/browse navigation, and the chrome (captions, table of contents) and fit-scale canvas.\\n3. **Presentation index** — the registry that maps each presentation to its own route so that multiple presentations coexist.\\n\\nDetection is contract-level, keyed on the presence of these anchors rather than a byte-identical scaffold, so cosmetic differences (file naming, formatting, extra dependencies) do not trigger re-scaffolding. When scaffolding, the skill SHALL NOT assume the required dependencies are already installed.\\n\\nThe scaffold SHALL be styling-framework-neutral and SHALL ship with zero presentation styling defaults. It SHALL install the runtime and build dependencies needed for React, Vite, TypeScript, Motion, Lucide icons, linting, and render verification, but it SHALL NOT require Tailwind, a Tailwind Vite plugin, a default CSS theme, default colors, default fonts, default card styles, default button styles, or any other styling framework. Styling systems MAY be added by the presentation author or host project after scaffolding.\\n\\nThe skill SHALL resolve scaffold templates relative to the skill file that declares them, so agents do not depend on the user's current working directory when locating `templates/bootstrap/` or presentation templates.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Empty or fully unscaffolded directory\\n- **WHEN** the skill runs in an empty directory or a project with none of the three anchors present\\n- **THEN** it performs a full scaffold (build setup, scene kit, and presentation index) and installs the required dependencies before creating the presentation\\n\\n#### Scenario: Already scaffolded\\n- **WHEN** all three anchors are already present\\n- **THEN** the skill skips scaffolding and proceeds directly to creating or modifying the presentation\\n\\n#### Scenario: Partial scaffold\\n- **WHEN** some but not all anchors are present\\n- **THEN** the skill scaffolds only the missing anchors (and their dependencies) without disturbing the ones already present\\n\\n#### Scenario: Scaffold does not impose a style system\\n- **WHEN** the skill scaffolds a presentation app\\n- **THEN** the generated app can build without Tailwind or another styling framework\\n- **AND** the scaffold does not define default presentation colors, fonts, spacing scale, card styles, button styles, borders, shadows, or CSS theme tokens\\n\\n#### Scenario: Templates resolve from skill directory\\n- **WHEN** the skill copies bootstrap or presentation templates\\n- **THEN** it resolves those paths relative to the skill's own `SKILL.md` directory\\n\\n#### Scenario: Monorepo target\\n- **WHEN** the skill runs inside a monorepo\\n- **THEN** it scaffolds the presentation app into a `presentations/` directory as its own self-contained app rather than at the repository root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Standalone project target\\n- **WHEN** the skill scaffolds in an empty or standalone (non-monorepo) project\\n- **THEN** it scaffolds the presentation app at the repository root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Non-empty project missing scaffolding\\n- **WHEN** the project is non-empty but lacks the scene kit or presentation index\\n- **THEN** the skill states the target location it will scaffold into and proceeds only after the user confirms\\n\\n### Requirement: Create a new presentation\\nThe skill SHALL generate a new presentation as a self-contained unit reachable at its own route and registered so that multiple presentations coexist.\\n\\n#### Scenario: New presentation is self-contained and routed\\n- **WHEN** a new presentation is created\\n- **THEN** it is written as its own folder, reachable at its own route, and registered in the presentation index\\n\\n#### Scenario: Presentation owns its visual style\\n- **WHEN** the skill creates a presentation with a designed visual look\\n- **THEN** the styling is added in files owned by that presentation or by the host app rather than in the reusable scene kit\\n- **AND** plain CSS is the default styling approach unless the host project already uses a styling framework or the user explicitly requests one\\n\\n#### Scenario: Existing presentations are preserved\\n- **WHEN** a new presentation is created and other presentations already exist\\n- **THEN** the existing presentations remain intact and reachable\\n\\n### Requirement: Modify an existing presentation\\nThe skill SHALL support modifying an existing presentation, identifying the target first and asking only about the requested changes.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Target unspecified or ambiguous\\n- **WHEN** the skill is asked to modify a presentation without a clear target\\n- **THEN** it lists the existing presentations and asks which to modify before changing anything\\n\\n#### Scenario: Scoped modification\\n- **WHEN** the target presentation is identified\\n- **THEN** the skill asks only about the requested changes (steps, entities, or style) and edits that presentation without re-walking the full create flow\\n\\n### Requirement: Self-verify before reporting completion\\nBefore reporting success, the skill SHALL confirm that the generated or modified presentation builds, renders without errors, and is visually coherent in a browser, fixing any failures itself. The render check SHALL at minimum render the presentation's first step without runtime or console errors; the full multi-step render check across every step is defined by the `presentation-verification` capability. The visual composition check SHALL inspect screenshots or an equivalent browser view of the first step, the last step, and any dense/key steps; responsive-sensitive presentations SHALL also be checked at a narrow viewport. When a project-local screenshot helper is available, the skill SHALL prefer it over ad hoc scripts outside the project tree so browser tooling resolves from local dependencies, settled screenshots are captured after animations complete, and advisory visual warnings can be reviewed.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Checks run before done\\n- **WHEN** the skill finishes generating or modifying a presentation\\n- **THEN** it runs the build, at least a first-step render check, and a browser visual composition check before reporting completion\\n\\n#### Scenario: Failures are fixed, not reported as success\\n- **WHEN** the build, render, or visual composition check fails\\n- **THEN** the skill fixes the issues and re-checks rather than reporting success\\n\\n### Requirement: Generated presentation quality bar\\nEvery generated presentation SHALL build with no type errors, render its first step without runtime errors, present a caption per step, support next/previous navigation, pass a visual composition check, and conform to the evolving-scene model.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Builds clean\\n- **WHEN** a presentation is generated\\n- **THEN** `npm run build` completes with no type errors\\n\\n#### Scenario: Renders without errors\\n- **WHEN** the presentation route is opened\\n- **THEN** it renders its first step with no runtime or console errors\\n\\n#### Scenario: Captions and navigation present\\n- **WHEN** viewing a presentation\\n- **THEN** each step shows a caption and the user can navigate to the next and previous steps\\n\\n#### Scenario: Visual composition is inspected\\n- **WHEN** a presentation is generated or modified\\n- **THEN** key browser screenshots or equivalent browser views show that important scene content fits the fixed canvas, intentional overlaps remain readable, and content does not collide with chrome such as captions, progress indicators, table of contents, or navigation controls\\n\\n#### Scenario: Screenshot helper is project-local\\n- **WHEN** the skill captures screenshots for visual inspection\\n- **THEN** it uses the scaffolded project-local helper when available, or otherwise writes any temporary Playwright helper under the project root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Visual warnings are reviewed\\n- **WHEN** the screenshot helper emits overlap or chrome-polish warnings\\n- **THEN** the skill reviews the referenced steps, fixes accidental collisions or indistinct current-step chrome, and marks only intentional readable overlaps as allowed\\n\\n#### Scenario: Active chrome and attribution are styled locally\\n- **WHEN** the generated presentation includes table-of-contents, progress, navigation, or attribution chrome\\n- **THEN** presentation-owned or host-owned CSS makes the active step visibly distinct and the attribution legible\\n- **AND** the reusable scene kit remains free of default colors, fonts, borders, button styles, and theme tokens\\n\""}],"label":"[harness frame or verified index]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":42,"end_line":42,"lines":[{"line":42,"text":" \"text\": \"## ADDED Requirements\\n\\n### Requirement: Build verification\\nVerification SHALL build the whole application — all presentations plus the index — and fail if the build does not succeed.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Build must succeed\\n- **WHEN** verification runs\\n- **THEN** it builds the whole app and fails if `npm run build` reports any type or build error\\n\\n### Requirement: Committed reference sample\\nA generated sample presentation SHALL be committed in the repository as a known-good example, registered and reachable like any other presentation.\\n\\nThe sample is the self-referential talk **\\\"How to Use This Skill to Make a Presentation\\\"** — a presentation, built by the skill, about building presentations with the skill. Its closing beat reveals that the viewer is looking at an example of the skill's own output. The sample SHALL implement the following steps (titles, captions, and scene intent are normative; the per-step visual design is deferred to design):\\n\\nThe sample is one continuously evolving scene: a conversation row (**you** ↔ **skill**) anchors the top, a tray of step cards accumulates below it, and later beats draw connections and a final reveal frame around what is already on screen. Entities accumulate; they are never rearranged or redrawn.\\n\\n| # | Era | Title (present) | Caption (browse) | Scene content |\\n|---|-----|-----------------|------------------|---------------|\\n| 1 | the ask | \\\"You have a topic\\\" | It starts with you, a topic, and mild overconfidence. | A **you** entity and a **prompt** bubble appear. |\\n| 2 | the ask | \\\"The skill interviews you\\\" | One question at a time: the topic, the look, then each beat of the story. | A **skill** node appears; a two-way arrow connects you↔skill with a **question chip** above it. |\\n| 3 | the gathering | \\\"Answers become steps\\\" | Each answer lands as a step card — title, caption, visual — plus what morphs from one step into the next. | A tray appears under the conversation; the first **step-card** lands in it, showing the parts every step carries (title, caption, visual). What morphs is drawn on the link between consecutive cards, not inside them. |\\n| 4 | the gathering | \\\"The deck grows\\\" | Same shapes, new beats. Every answer extends the story without redrawing it. | More step-cards land in the tray; everything already on screen stays put. |\\n| 5 | the gathering | \\\"You set the depth\\\" | Spell out every step, or sketch a few and see how it looks. You hold the gate. | A dashed **ghost card** marks unspecified steps; a partial↔full control docks on **you**. |\\n| 6 | the build | \\\"It assembles the scene\\\" | Your steps are wired into one evolving scene, drawn with a shared scene kit — ready-made boxes, arrows, and motion that make entities morph. | The **scene-kit** socket plugs into the bottom edge of the assembled tray of step cards (the tray is not framed); its label names the shared kit the scene is drawn with. |\\n| 7 | the build | \\\"It checks its own work\\\" | Before saying done, it builds and renders every step — and fixes what breaks. | A **verify** node is chained after the step cards in the same tray row (verification is part of the skill's own pipeline); build + render checks resolve to a green pass check on it. |\\n| 8 | the loop | \\\"Changed your mind? Loop it.\\\" | Point at a step and ask. The skill edits the scene in place — nothing is redrawn from scratch. | A **modify** arc reaches from the conversation down into the route; the edited card is flagged. |\\n| 9 | the reveal | \\\"You're looking at one\\\" | This presentation was built exactly this way. Thanks for watching. | An outer frame draws around the whole diagram, labeled — self-reference reveal. |\\n\\n<!-- deferred-to-design: per-step visual design — exact entity shapes, layout coordinates, layoutId namespace, colors, and motion timing — is settled in the design stage. The steps, titles, captions, and scene intent above are fixed. -->\\n\\n#### Scenario: Sample exists and matches the outline\\n- **WHEN** verification runs\\n- **THEN** it confirms the committed reference sample presentation exists, is registered/reachable, and implements the nine steps above in order\\n\\n#### Scenario: Missing sample fails\\n- **WHEN** the reference sample is absent\\n- **THEN** verification fails\\n\\n### Requirement: Render verification\\nVerification SHALL render the reference sample through all of its steps and fail if any step produces a runtime or console error. The render check runs the sample in a real browser against a production preview and steps through every step. The preview server and browser navigation SHALL use a deterministic IPv4 loopback address (`127.0.0.1`) so verification does not depend on how `localhost` resolves in the runtime environment. (Mechanism settled in design: `vite preview` + a Playwright/Chromium driver that enumerates steps via the chrome's step-count hook.)\\n\\n#### Scenario: Every step renders cleanly\\n- **WHEN** verification renders the sample\\n- **THEN** it steps through every step and asserts each renders without runtime or console errors\\n\\n#### Scenario: Preview uses IPv4 loopback\\n- **WHEN** verification starts the production preview and opens presentation routes\\n- **THEN** the preview host, readiness probe, and browser URLs use `127.0.0.1` consistently\\n\\n#### Scenario: Console or page error fails verification\\n- **WHEN** the sample emits a console error or an uncaught page error while stepping through it\\n- **THEN** verification fails and identifies the failing step\\n\\n#### Scenario: Step error fails verification\\n- **WHEN** any step errors during render\\n- **THEN** verification fails and identifies the failing step\\n\\n### Requirement: Pass/fail reporting\\nVerification SHALL produce an unambiguous pass/fail outcome suitable for automated checks.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Clear outcome\\n- **WHEN** verification completes\\n- **THEN** it reports a clear pass or fail (non-zero exit on failure) identifying which check failed\\n\\n### Requirement: Visual inspection artifacts\\nScaffolded projects SHALL provide a project-local helper that captures per-step screenshots from a production preview for human visual review. The helper SHALL wait for step transition animations to settle before each screenshot and SHALL surface advisory warnings for suspicious text/chrome collisions, visually indistinct active navigation states, and unpolished attribution. The helper supports the skill's visual composition check, but its screenshots and warnings are inspection artifacts rather than automated pass/fail evidence.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Capture step screenshots\\n- **WHEN** the screenshot helper runs for a registered presentation\\n- **THEN** it captures each step at a standard desktop viewport and writes the images under a predictable project-local artifact directory\\n\\n#### Scenario: Screenshots are settled\\n- **WHEN** the helper advances from one step to the next\\n- **THEN** it waits for the configured settle interval before capturing the next screenshot\\n\\n#### Scenario: Suspicious overlap is reported\\n- **WHEN** visible text or presentation chrome overlaps another visible text/chrome element without an explicit allow-overlap marker\\n- **THEN** the helper prints an advisory warning identifying the step and overlapping elements\\n\\n#### Scenario: Intentional overlap can be marked\\n- **WHEN** a presentation marks a subtree as allowing overlap\\n- **THEN** the helper does not report overlap warnings for elements inside that subtree\\n\\n#### Scenario: Indistinct active chrome is reported\\n- **WHEN** the active progress indicator or active table-of-contents entry is visually indistinguishable from inactive controls\\n- **THEN** the helper prints an advisory warning identifying the affected chrome\\n\\n#### Scenario: Unpolished attribution is reported\\n- **WHEN** the attribution link appears too small or browser-default\\n- **THEN** the helper prints an advisory warning pointing authors to the attribution styling hook\\n\""}],"label":"[harness frame or verified index]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":1008,"end_line":1012,"lines":[{"line":1008,"text":"### Step E1 — Materialization materialize the same bootstrap anchors; its package will install/build in isolation and the sample route will pass browser verification."},{"line":1011,"text":"- **Observation:** Helper copied files Warning behavior is described in report evidence and not counted as the wide reference overlap defect."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-1235bdc5eff5d034 (exploration-log)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":766,"end_line":795,"lines":[{"line":766,"text":"## Narrow viewport readability threshold"},{"line":767,"text":""},{"line":768,"text":"**Question:** The approved design requires the diagram to scale uniformly to fit the fixed 880 × 380 canvas. AT-003 additionally expects important content to remain readable at a narrow viewport. At 390 × 844, the scene fits at scale 0.389 and its card labels become very small. What minimum readable size or behavior should govern narrow viewports?"},{"line":769,"text":""},{"line":770,"text":"**Observed evidence:** `acceptance-screenshots/step-05-dense-narrow-052e4093.png`, `step-01-first-narrow-052e4093.png`, and `step-09-last-narrow-052e4093.png`; live DOM reports `data-scale=\"0.3886363636363636\"` while retaining `880px × 380px` canvas geometry."},{"line":771,"text":""},{"line":772,"text":"**Options and consequences:** Keep strict uniform scaling and accept that detailed labels are hard to read on narrow phones; allow a minimum scale and overflow/zoom, which may no longer fit the entire scene; or define a separate narrow presentation treatment, which risks changing the fixed canvas's internal composition. I have recorded a usability defect against the test-plan readability expectation; the product/design threshold and acceptable narrow-view behavior remain for human review."},{"line":773,"text":""},{"line":774,"text":"## Acceptance round 0, F-002: header overlap warnings that are not visually present"},{"line":775,"text":""},{"line":776,"text":"**Question:** The tester reproduced two overlap warnings on every sample step at 1440 × 900: the mode toggle against the marker and against the document title. The screenshots show clear separation. Is this a defect?"},{"line":777,"text":""},{"line":778,"text":"**Requirement:**"},{"line":779,"text":"- `specs/presentation-verification/spec.md`, \"Suspicious overlap is reported\": warn when \"visible text or presentation chrome overlaps another visible text/chrome element\"."},{"line":780,"text":"- Ruling \"Overlap diagnostics\" above made chrome-element rectangles a party to the check."},{"line":781,"text":""},{"line":782,"text":"**Ruling:** It is a defect in my implementation of that ruling, not a spec question. I collected the border box of every chrome hook. The marker and document title are block-level elements whose boxes span the whole header (x=24…1416) although their glyphs are left-aligned, so the box intersected the right-aligned toggle. Fix: chrome that is not a `button` or `a` and contains visible text no longer contributes a box, because its glyph rectangles are already collected. Interactive controls keep their padded box, and text-less chrome such as an icon-only brand keeps its box. The earlier ruling still holds for the cases it was written for."},{"line":783,"text":""},{"line":784,"text":"**Rationale:** An advisory warning that fires on every step of the committed sample would train authors to ignore the list, and the skill's warning-review loop would chase non-collisions. The spec wording (\"visible text/chrome element\") is satisfied by the visible glyphs of text chrome."},{"line":785,"text":""},{"line":786,"text":"**Evidence:**"},{"line":787,"text":"- Regression test \"I-45 block-level text chrome uses glyph bounds while interactive chrome keeps its padded box\" in `tests/scripts.test.ts`, run with `evidence/F-002-unit.log` (10 of 10 pass)."},{"line":788,"text":"- The same test fails against the pre-fix `scripts/diagnostics.mjs`: `evidence/F-002-unit-prefix.log` shows the marker and title boxes collected."},{"line":789,"text":"- `evidence/F-002-lint.log` and `evidence/F-002-types.log` are clean."},{"line":790,"text":"- The root script and the bootstrap template copy are byte-identical."},{"line":791,"text":""},{"line":792,"text":"**Integration regression recommendation:** INT-002 should gain a header-like fixture (a full-width block marker with a right-aligned button) that asserts no overlap warning in real browser geometry. I did not add it because integration and end-to-end suites were not to be run in this step, and an unrun browser test could break the next round. It is a meaningful addition for a later pass."},{"line":793,"text":""},{"line":794,"text":"**Pending from the user:** None."},{"line":795,"text":""}],"label":"[artifact candidate-0c74b4fc9e9bc4f7 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":796,"end_line":821,"lines":[{"line":796,"text":"## Acceptance round 0, F-001: sample diagram text is 5 to 7 CSS pixels at a 390-pixel viewport"},{"line":797,"text":""},{"line":798,"text":"**Question:** At 390 × 844 the 880 × 380 canvas scales to about 0.389, so the card titles and labels render at roughly 5 to 7 CSS pixels. AT-003 expects \"important content remains readable ... at both viewport widths\". Should this be fixed?"},{"line":799,"text":""},{"line":800,"text":"**Requirement:**"},{"line":801,"text":"- `specs/evolving-scene-presentations/spec.md`, \"Fixed-canvas fit scaling\": the diagram is \"scaled uniformly to fit the available viewport, so the composition does not reflow\". \"The default design canvas SHALL be 880 × 380, with per-mode fit geometry for the browse and present layouts.\""},{"line":802,"text":"- Same file, \"Uniform scaling on resize\": scaling is uniform with no reflow of the internal composition."},{"line":803,"text":"- `design.md` Stage: scale is constant within a mode so `layoutId` morphs stay clean."},{"line":804,"text":"- `test-plan.md` AT-003 asks for readable content and a narrow-viewport pass."},{"line":805,"text":"- The sample's typography and geometry are deferred to design, and the sample must keep entities stationary across beats."},{"line":806,"text":""},{"line":807,"text":"**Ruling:** No code change, and I am escalating. The scale is determined by the approved fixed canvas: (390 − 2 × 24) / 880 = 0.389. Reaching comfortable text at that width needs one of:"},{"line":808,"text":"1. A different canvas or a narrow-viewport layout, which departs from the approved \"uniform scaling, no reflow\" requirement and the \"880 × 380 default\" requirement."},{"line":809,"text":"2. A per-viewport sample layout, which breaks the \"entities are never rearranged\" sample requirement unless a second composition is authored."},{"line":810,"text":"3. Larger sample typography on the existing geometry. That is within the presentation's own design latitude, but the cards are 132 × 86 and the smallest labels are already 9 to 12 px. Even 16 px design text renders at about 6 px, so it cannot meet a comfortable reading size, and I cannot confirm in this step that larger text would fit the cards without new collisions."},{"line":811,"text":""},{"line":812,"text":"I did not change the margin or typography. The change would be marginal (the margin saves a few percent of scale) and cannot reach comfortable readability, and it adds unverified risk."},{"line":813,"text":""},{"line":814,"text":"**Rationale:** The observation is correct, but it follows from approved requirements. The narrow-view expectation in AT-003 and the fixed-canvas requirement can only both hold if \"readable\" is read as \"legible when zoomed or as part of a scaled whole\", which is a product decision."},{"line":815,"text":""},{"line":816,"text":"**Pending from the user (decision needed):** Choose one:"},{"line":817,"text":"- (a) Accept the uniform-scale behavior at phone widths as intended. AT-003's narrow-view clause is then interpreted as \"fits without reflow or collision\"."},{"line":818,"text":"- (b) Approve a narrow-viewport mechanism (a second per-mode canvas, a minimum scale with scrolling, or an authored narrow composition). That changes the fixed-canvas and no-reflow requirements and needs a spec update."},{"line":819,"text":"- (c) Approve modest typography increases in the sample only, accepting that this will not reach comfortable readability at 390 px."},{"line":820,"text":""},{"line":821,"text":"Until the user decides, the implementation stays as is."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-0c74b4fc9e9bc4f7 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":823,"end_line":847,"lines":[{"line":823,"text":"## Acceptance round 1, F-003: styled text-bearing chrome was dropped from overlap checks"},{"line":824,"text":""},{"line":825,"text":"**Question:** The round 0 fix for F-002 stopped collecting the box of non-interactive chrome whenever it contained visible text. The tester showed that a host brand styled as a bordered, semi-transparent 240 × 80 px box can sit on a scene label (\"you\") and produce no warning, because only its \"HOST BRAND\" glyphs were compared. Is this a defect?"},{"line":826,"text":""},{"line":827,"text":"**Requirement:**"},{"line":828,"text":"- `specs/presentation-verification/spec.md`, \"Suspicious overlap is reported\": warn when \"visible text or presentation chrome overlaps another visible text/chrome element\"."},{"line":829,"text":"- My ruling \"Overlap diagnostics\" above made chrome elements a party to the check."},{"line":830,"text":""},{"line":831,"text":"**Ruling:** It is a defect. My F-002 fix was too broad. A box is visible chrome only when it is decorated, so the rule is now:"},{"line":832,"text":"- Non-interactive text chrome contributes its box if its computed style has a non-transparent background, a border with non-zero width and a style other than none, or a box shadow. Otherwise it contributes only its glyph rectangles, which is the F-002 case (an unstyled block-level marker or title spanning the header)."},{"line":833,"text":"- Buttons and links always contribute their box, as before."},{"line":834,"text":"- Text-less chrome keeps its box, as before."},{"line":835,"text":"- The sample's marker, title and caption carry no decoration, so the F-002 result is preserved."},{"line":836,"text":""},{"line":837,"text":"**Rationale:** Padding on an undecorated element is invisible, so glyph bounds are its visible extent. A visible background, border or shadow makes the whole rectangle part of what the viewer sees. This keeps the false positive from F-002 away and restores the collision the spec asks for."},{"line":838,"text":""},{"line":839,"text":"**Evidence:**"},{"line":840,"text":"- `tests/scripts.test.ts`, \"I-45 decorated text chrome keeps its visible box so a styled brand colliding with scene text warns\". It covers a background, a border, and a fully transparent background (no box)."},{"line":841,"text":"- `evidence/F-003-unit.log` shows 11 of 11 passing. `evidence/F-003-unit-prefix.log` shows the new case failing against the previous script."},{"line":842,"text":"- `evidence/F-003-lint.log` and `evidence/F-003-types.log` are clean."},{"line":843,"text":"- The root script and the bootstrap template copy are byte-identical."},{"line":844,"text":""},{"line":845,"text":"**Integration regression recommendation:** INT-002 should add a styled-brand fixture whose box overlaps scene text and a plain full-width marker next to a right-aligned button, asserting a warning for the first and none for the second in real browser geometry. Not added now because integration suites are not run in this step."},{"line":846,"text":""},{"line":847,"text":"**Pending from the user:** None."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-0c74b4fc9e9bc4f7 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":934,"end_line":968,"lines":[{"line":934,"text":"## F-001 — Diagram labels are too small at the narrow viewport (reproduced in round 1)"},{"line":935,"text":""},{"line":936,"text":"- **Affected behavior:** Responsive composition of the reference presentation."},{"line":937,"text":"- **Expected:** AT-003 expects important scene content to remain readable at a narrow viewport while the 880 × 380 design canvas scales uniformly."},{"line":938,"text":"- **Observed:** At 390 × 844 the canvas has `data-scale=\"0.3886363636363636\"`; card titles and labels are reduced to roughly 5–7 CSS pixels and are difficult to read. The outer scene fits without reflow or collisions, but the meaningful diagram text does not remain comfortably readable."},{"line":939,"text":"- **Reproduction:** Open `http://127.0.0.1:4173/how-to-make-a-presentation`, resize to 390 × 844, and inspect step 5. Also visible on steps 1 and 9."},{"line":940,"text":"- **Evidence:** `acceptance-screenshots/step-05-dense-narrow-052e4093.png`, `step-01-first-narrow-052e4093.png`, `step-09-last-narrow-052e4093.png`; narrow scale and 880 × 380 canvas were read from the live DOM through AXI. The screenshots show the diagram's small text against readable surrounding chrome."},{"line":941,"text":""},{"line":942,"text":"## F-002 — Inspection helper reports header overlaps that are not visually present (fixed in round 1)"},{"line":943,"text":""},{"line":944,"text":"- **Affected behavior:** Advisory overlap diagnostics for the sample at wide viewports."},{"line":945,"text":"- **Expected:** Warnings identify suspicious visible text/chrome collisions that a reviewer should inspect."},{"line":946,"text":"- **Observed:** The helper reports two overlaps on every one of the nine steps: the mode toggle with the marker and the document title. Live geometry for the header hooks and toggle was queried with AXI at step 7."},{"line":949,"text":""},{"line":950,"text":"### Round 1 retest result for F-002"},{"line":951,"text":""},{"line":952,"text":"At `8088dbc96e39193a2af6d9a2dc375a623c925b1f`, `npm run inspect -- how-to-make-a-presentation` reported no warnings on any of nine steps at either 1440 × 900 or 390 × 844. The step-1 report has no warnings despite the visible collision."},{"line":960,"text":"- **Evidence:** `round-1-brand-padding-probe-report.json` (all nine steps have empty warnings); `acceptance-screenshots/brand-padding-probe-8088dbc9.png` (brand rectangle overlaps the “you” node); scratch reproduction source at `/workspace/home/.agent-runner/projects/-artifacts--runtime-candidate-worktree/runs/implement-change-2026-10-26T03-32-14-991527899Z/scratch/acceptance-test/round-1/repo/src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/Talk.tsx` and `presentation.css`; AXI geometry at scale 1: brand bounds `[550,248,790,328]`, “you” glyph bounds `[576.2,278.5,643.8,301]`."},{"line":961,"text":""},{"line":962,"text":""},{"line":963,"text":"## Round 2 retest — revision 6aa6e9fe3ed951f1a9de55cd0bd80ea96eb749af"},{"line":964,"text":""},{"line":965,"text":"- F-001 persists: Reproduced at 390 × 844 on step 5. Evidence: round-2-baseline-wide-report.json."},{"line":967,"text":"- F-003 fixed in this revision: Both semitransparent-background and border-only host brand box collisions now warn against visible scene text; transparent, undecorated box with separate text has no warnings. Evidence: round-2-brand-decorated-report.json, round-2-brand-border-report.json, round-2-brand-transparent-report.json, and acceptance-screenshots/brand-border-probe-r2-wide-6aa6e9fe.png."},{"line":968,"text":""}],"label":"[artifact candidate-5ca30e5cbddd84ee (findings-history)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":1342,"end_line":1343,"lines":[{"line":1342,"text":" Start at 04:29:45"},{"line":1343,"text":" Duration 1.61s (transform 113ms, setup 130ms, import 441ms, tests 243ms, environment 629ms)"}],"label":"[artifact candidate-fe1448d2aec11ac5 (referenced-material)]"}],"assumption-decisions-and-escalations-proportionate":[{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":38,"end_line":38,"lines":[{"line":38,"text":" \"text\": \"## ADDED Requirements\\n\\n### Requirement: Interactive requirement gathering\\nThe skill SHALL gather presentation details by asking the user clarifying questions one at a time — covering the topic, the visual style, and the content and visual description of each step. The user controls how much to specify; the skill SHALL NOT assume details the user can still provide, but SHALL allow the user to proceed with partial detail and iterate. The skill MAY, at its discretion, draw ASCII mockups to represent key or complex steps when doing so helps confirm the intended visual layout.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Prompt is missing details\\n- **WHEN** the skill is invoked with a prompt that omits the topic, visual style, or per-step descriptions\\n- **THEN** the skill asks for the missing information one question at a time rather than assuming it\\n\\n#### Scenario: User proceeds with partial detail\\n- **WHEN** the user chooses to build after providing only some details\\n- **THEN** the skill generates a presentation from what was captured without blocking on a hard completeness gate\\n\\n#### Scenario: Prompt already complete\\n- **WHEN** the prompt already contains the topic, style, and all step details\\n- **THEN** the skill may proceed to build without further questions\\n\\n#### Scenario: ASCII mockup for a complex step\\n- **WHEN** a step's visual layout is key or complex\\n- **THEN** the skill may present an ASCII mockup of that step to the user to confirm the layout before building, without doing so for every step\\n\\n### Requirement: Self-bootstrapping scaffold\\nBefore creating or modifying a presentation, the skill SHALL ensure the project provides the infrastructure a generated presentation depends on, SHALL resolve where that infrastructure belongs, and SHALL scaffold whatever is missing — including installing the dependencies the infrastructure requires. The required infrastructure is three contract anchors:\\n\\n1. **Build setup** — a Vite + React + TypeScript app with a working `npm run build`.\\n2. **Scene kit** — the reusable, presentation-agnostic engine: the `Step`/`Scene` step contract, the stage/host that mounts the active step and runs entity morphs, the present/browse navigation, and the chrome (captions, table of contents) and fit-scale canvas.\\n3. **Presentation index** — the registry that maps each presentation to its own route so that multiple presentations coexist.\\n\\nDetection is contract-level, keyed on the presence of these anchors rather than a byte-identical scaffold, so cosmetic differences (file naming, formatting, extra dependencies) do not trigger re-scaffolding. When scaffolding, the skill SHALL NOT assume the required dependencies are already installed.\\n\\nThe scaffold SHALL be styling-framework-neutral and SHALL ship with zero presentation styling defaults. It SHALL install the runtime and build dependencies needed for React, Vite, TypeScript, Motion, Lucide icons, linting, and render verification, but it SHALL NOT require Tailwind, a Tailwind Vite plugin, a default CSS theme, default colors, default fonts, default card styles, default button styles, or any other styling framework. Styling systems MAY be added by the presentation author or host project after scaffolding.\\n\\nThe skill SHALL resolve scaffold templates relative to the skill file that declares them, so agents do not depend on the user's current working directory when locating `templates/bootstrap/` or presentation templates.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Empty or fully unscaffolded directory\\n- **WHEN** the skill runs in an empty directory or a project with none of the three anchors present\\n- **THEN** it performs a full scaffold (build setup, scene kit, and presentation index) and installs the required dependencies before creating the presentation\\n\\n#### Scenario: Already scaffolded\\n- **WHEN** all three anchors are already present\\n- **THEN** the skill skips scaffolding and proceeds directly to creating or modifying the presentation\\n\\n#### Scenario: Partial scaffold\\n- **WHEN** some but not all anchors are present\\n- **THEN** the skill scaffolds only the missing anchors (and their dependencies) without disturbing the ones already present\\n\\n#### Scenario: Scaffold does not impose a style system\\n- **WHEN** the skill scaffolds a presentation app\\n- **THEN** the generated app can build without Tailwind or another styling framework\\n- **AND** the scaffold does not define default presentation colors, fonts, spacing scale, card styles, button styles, borders, shadows, or CSS theme tokens\\n\\n#### Scenario: Templates resolve from skill directory\\n- **WHEN** the skill copies bootstrap or presentation templates\\n- **THEN** it resolves those paths relative to the skill's own `SKILL.md` directory\\n\\n#### Scenario: Monorepo target\\n- **WHEN** the skill runs inside a monorepo\\n- **THEN** it scaffolds the presentation app into a `presentations/` directory as its own self-contained app rather than at the repository root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Standalone project target\\n- **WHEN** the skill scaffolds in an empty or standalone (non-monorepo) project\\n- **THEN** it scaffolds the presentation app at the repository root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Non-empty project missing scaffolding\\n- **WHEN** the project is non-empty but lacks the scene kit or presentation index\\n- **THEN** the skill states the target location it will scaffold into and proceeds only after the user confirms\\n\\n### Requirement: Create a new presentation\\nThe skill SHALL generate a new presentation as a self-contained unit reachable at its own route and registered so that multiple presentations coexist.\\n\\n#### Scenario: New presentation is self-contained and routed\\n- **WHEN** a new presentation is created\\n- **THEN** it is written as its own folder, reachable at its own route, and registered in the presentation index\\n\\n#### Scenario: Presentation owns its visual style\\n- **WHEN** the skill creates a presentation with a designed visual look\\n- **THEN** the styling is added in files owned by that presentation or by the host app rather than in the reusable scene kit\\n- **AND** plain CSS is the default styling approach unless the host project already uses a styling framework or the user explicitly requests one\\n\\n#### Scenario: Existing presentations are preserved\\n- **WHEN** a new presentation is created and other presentations already exist\\n- **THEN** the existing presentations remain intact and reachable\\n\\n### Requirement: Modify an existing presentation\\nThe skill SHALL support modifying an existing presentation, identifying the target first and asking only about the requested changes.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Target unspecified or ambiguous\\n- **WHEN** the skill is asked to modify a presentation without a clear target\\n- **THEN** it lists the existing presentations and asks which to modify before changing anything\\n\\n#### Scenario: Scoped modification\\n- **WHEN** the target presentation is identified\\n- **THEN** the skill asks only about the requested changes (steps, entities, or style) and edits that presentation without re-walking the full create flow\\n\\n### Requirement: Self-verify before reporting completion\\nBefore reporting success, the skill SHALL confirm that the generated or modified presentation builds, renders without errors, and is visually coherent in a browser, fixing any failures itself. The render check SHALL at minimum render the presentation's first step without runtime or console errors; the full multi-step render check across every step is defined by the `presentation-verification` capability. The visual composition check SHALL inspect screenshots or an equivalent browser view of the first step, the last step, and any dense/key steps; responsive-sensitive presentations SHALL also be checked at a narrow viewport. When a project-local screenshot helper is available, the skill SHALL prefer it over ad hoc scripts outside the project tree so browser tooling resolves from local dependencies, settled screenshots are captured after animations complete, and advisory visual warnings can be reviewed.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Checks run before done\\n- **WHEN** the skill finishes generating or modifying a presentation\\n- **THEN** it runs the build, at least a first-step render check, and a browser visual composition check before reporting completion\\n\\n#### Scenario: Failures are fixed, not reported as success\\n- **WHEN** the build, render, or visual composition check fails\\n- **THEN** the skill fixes the issues and re-checks rather than reporting success\\n\\n### Requirement: Generated presentation quality bar\\nEvery generated presentation SHALL build with no type errors, render its first step without runtime errors, present a caption per step, support next/previous navigation, pass a visual composition check, and conform to the evolving-scene model.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Builds clean\\n- **WHEN** a presentation is generated\\n- **THEN** `npm run build` completes with no type errors\\n\\n#### Scenario: Renders without errors\\n- **WHEN** the presentation route is opened\\n- **THEN** it renders its first step with no runtime or console errors\\n\\n#### Scenario: Captions and navigation present\\n- **WHEN** viewing a presentation\\n- **THEN** each step shows a caption and the user can navigate to the next and previous steps\\n\\n#### Scenario: Visual composition is inspected\\n- **WHEN** a presentation is generated or modified\\n- **THEN** key browser screenshots or equivalent browser views show that important scene content fits the fixed canvas, intentional overlaps remain readable, and content does not collide with chrome such as captions, progress indicators, table of contents, or navigation controls\\n\\n#### Scenario: Screenshot helper is project-local\\n- **WHEN** the skill captures screenshots for visual inspection\\n- **THEN** it uses the scaffolded project-local helper when available, or otherwise writes any temporary Playwright helper under the project root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Visual warnings are reviewed\\n- **WHEN** the screenshot helper emits overlap or chrome-polish warnings\\n- **THEN** the skill reviews the referenced steps, fixes accidental collisions or indistinct current-step chrome, and marks only intentional readable overlaps as allowed\\n\\n#### Scenario: Active chrome and attribution are styled locally\\n- **WHEN** the generated presentation includes table-of-contents, progress, navigation, or attribution chrome\\n- **THEN** presentation-owned or host-owned CSS makes the active step visibly distinct and
