index]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":42,"end_line":42,"lines":[{"line":42,"text":" \"text\": \"## ADDED Requirements\\n\\n### Requirement: Build verification\\nVerification SHALL build the whole application — all presentations plus the index — and fail if the build does not succeed.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Build must succeed\\n- **WHEN** verification runs\\n- **THEN** it builds the whole app and fails if `npm run build` reports any type or build error\\n\\n### Requirement: Committed reference sample\\nA generated sample presentation SHALL be committed in the repository as a known-good example, registered and reachable like any other presentation.\\n\\nThe sample is the self-referential talk **\\\"How to Use This Skill to Make a Presentation\\\"** — a presentation, built by the skill, about building presentations with the skill. Its closing beat reveals that the viewer is looking at an example of the skill's own output. The sample SHALL implement the following steps (titles, captions, and scene intent are normative; the per-step visual design is deferred to design):\\n\\nThe sample is one continuously evolving scene: a conversation row (**you** ↔ **skill**) anchors the top, a tray of step cards accumulates below it, and later beats draw connections and a final reveal frame around what is already on screen. Entities accumulate; they are never rearranged or redrawn.\\n\\n| # | Era | Title (present) | Caption (browse) | Scene content |\\n|---|-----|-----------------|------------------|---------------|\\n| 1 | the ask | \\\"You have a topic\\\" | It starts with you, a topic, and mild overconfidence. | A **you** entity and a **prompt** bubble appear. |\\n| 2 | the ask | \\\"The skill interviews you\\\" | One question at a time: the topic, the look, then each beat of the story. | A **skill** node appears; a two-way arrow connects you↔skill with a **question chip** above it. |\\n| 3 | the gathering | \\\"Answers become steps\\\" | Each answer lands as a step card — title, caption, visual — plus what morphs from one step into the next. | A tray appears under the conversation; the first **step-card** lands in it, showing the parts every step carries (title, caption, visual). What morphs is drawn on the link between consecutive cards, not inside them. |\\n| 4 | the gathering | \\\"The deck grows\\\" | Same shapes, new beats. Every answer extends the story without redrawing it. | More step-cards land in the tray; everything already on screen stays put. |\\n| 5 | the gathering | \\\"You set the depth\\\" | Spell out every step, or sketch a few and see how it looks. You hold the gate. | A dashed **ghost card** marks unspecified steps; a partial↔full control docks on **you**. |\\n| 6 | the build | \\\"It assembles the scene\\\" | Your steps are wired into one evolving scene, drawn with a shared scene kit — ready-made boxes, arrows, and motion that make entities morph. | The **scene-kit** socket plugs into the bottom edge of the assembled tray of step cards (the tray is not framed); its label names the shared kit the scene is drawn with. |\\n| 7 | the build | \\\"It checks its own work\\\" | Before saying done, it builds and renders every step — and fixes what breaks. | A **verify** node is chained after the step cards in the same tray row (verification is part of the skill's own pipeline); build + render checks resolve to a green pass check on it. |\\n| 8 | the loop | \\\"Changed your mind? Loop it.\\\" | Point at a step and ask. The skill edits the scene in place — nothing is redrawn from scratch. | A **modify** arc reaches from the conversation down into the route; the edited card is flagged. |\\n| 9 | the reveal | \\\"You're looking at one\\\" | This presentation was built exactly this way. Thanks for watching. | An outer frame draws around the whole diagram, labeled — self-reference reveal. |\\n\\n<!-- deferred-to-design: per-step visual design — exact entity shapes, layout coordinates, layoutId namespace, colors, and motion timing — is settled in the design stage. The steps, titles, captions, and scene intent above are fixed. -->\\n\\n#### Scenario: Sample exists and matches the outline\\n- **WHEN** verification runs\\n- **THEN** it confirms the committed reference sample presentation exists, is registered/reachable, and implements the nine steps above in order\\n\\n#### Scenario: Missing sample fails\\n- **WHEN** the reference sample is absent\\n- **THEN** verification fails\\n\\n### Requirement: Render verification\\nVerification SHALL render the reference sample through all of its steps and fail if any step produces a runtime or console error. The render check runs the sample in a real browser against a production preview and steps through every step. The preview server and browser navigation SHALL use a deterministic IPv4 loopback address (`127.0.0.1`) so verification does not depend on how `localhost` resolves in the runtime environment. (Mechanism settled in design: `vite preview` + a Playwright/Chromium driver that enumerates steps via the chrome's step-count hook.)\\n\\n#### Scenario: Every step renders cleanly\\n- **WHEN** verification renders the sample\\n- **THEN** it steps through every step and asserts each renders without runtime or console errors\\n\\n#### Scenario: Preview uses IPv4 loopback\\n- **WHEN** verification starts the production preview and opens presentation routes\\n- **THEN** the preview host, readiness probe, and browser URLs use `127.0.0.1` consistently\\n\\n#### Scenario: Console or page error fails verification\\n- **WHEN** the sample emits a console error or an uncaught page error while stepping through it\\n- **THEN** verification fails and identifies the failing step\\n\\n#### Scenario: Step error fails verification\\n- **WHEN** any step errors during render\\n- **THEN** verification fails and identifies the failing step\\n\\n### Requirement: Pass/fail reporting\\nVerification SHALL produce an unambiguous pass/fail outcome suitable for automated checks.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Clear outcome\\n- **WHEN** verification completes\\n- **THEN** it reports a clear pass or fail (non-zero exit on failure) identifying which check failed\\n\\n### Requirement: Visual inspection artifacts\\nScaffolded projects SHALL provide a project-local helper that captures per-step screenshots from a production preview for human visual review. The helper SHALL wait for step transition animations to settle before each screenshot and SHALL surface advisory warnings for suspicious text/chrome collisions, visually indistinct active navigation states, and unpolished attribution. The helper supports the skill's visual composition check, but its screenshots and warnings are inspection artifacts rather than automated pass/fail evidence.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Capture step screenshots\\n- **WHEN** the screenshot helper runs for a registered presentation\\n- **THEN** it captures each step at a standard desktop viewport and writes the images under a predictable project-local artifact directory\\n\\n#### Scenario: Screenshots are settled\\n- **WHEN** the helper advances from one step to the next\\n- **THEN** it waits for the configured settle interval before capturing the next screenshot\\n\\n#### Scenario: Suspicious overlap is reported\\n- **WHEN** visible text or presentation chrome overlaps another visible text/chrome element without an explicit allow-overlap marker\\n- **THEN** the helper prints an advisory warning identifying the step and overlapping elements\\n\\n#### Scenario: Intentional overlap can be marked\\n- **WHEN** a presentation marks a subtree as allowing overlap\\n- **THEN** the helper does not report overlap warnings for elements inside that subtree\\n\\n#### Scenario: Indistinct active chrome is reported\\n- **WHEN** the active progress indicator or active table-of-contents entry is visually indistinguishable from inactive controls\\n- **THEN** the helper prints an advisory warning identifying the affected chrome\\n\\n#### Scenario: Unpolished attribution is reported\\n- **WHEN** the attribution link appears too small or browser-default\\n- **THEN** the helper prints an advisory warning pointing authors to the attribution styling hook\\n\""}],"label":"[harness frame or verified index]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":663,"end_line":680,"lines":[{"line":663,"text":"4. The AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md instruction to do AXI inspection and screenshot review before completion is a project working instruction. It is not part of the approved definition (proposal, design, specs, test plan, checklist). The current user's explicit prohibition on operating the product and inspecting screenshots takes precedence for this run."},{"line":664,"text":" - Do not run `chrome-devtools-axi`."},{"line":665,"text":" - Do not open or read any screenshot the helper writes."},{"line":666,"text":" - Do not run agent acceptance flows (AT-001 to AT-004)."},{"line":667,"text":"5. Leave visual acceptance to the independent tester. Implement the project-local screenshot helper and its automated INT-002 test. Running the automated suites (`npm test`, the integration/e2e script, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm run verify`) is allowed. They are scripted pass/fail gates, not manual operation of the product, and their screenshot output must not be viewed."},{"line":668,"text":" - INT-002 must assert on the files written and on the diagnostics, not on how the image looks."},{"line":669,"text":"6. This does not change an approved requirement. I-28 and I-29 require the skill to instruct the agent to review the output visually. They do not require the implementor to do that review for this repository."},{"line":670,"text":""},{"line":671,"text":"**Rationale:**"},{"line":672,"text":"- It follows the plain wording of the checklist, `implement-change` and the current instruction, and it weakens none of them."},{"line":673,"text":"- The test plan puts browser-based visual quality and skill behavior under agent acceptance (AT-003 and AT-004), a separate stage, and requires INT-002 and E2E-001/E2E-002 for the deterministic parts."},{"line":674,"text":"- The prohibition on prompt-text tests exists because text matching proves nothing about how an agent behaves, so reading is the appropriate check."},{"line":675,"text":""},{"line":676,"text":"**Pending from the user:**"},{"line":677,"text":"- No decision is needed to proceed."},{"line":678,"text":"- The completion report must say plainly that the implementor did no AXI inspection and no screenshot review, and that this was left to the independent tester under the current instruction. CLAUDE.md's \"inspect representative steps with AXI and the project-local screenshot helper\" requirement is therefore unmet by the implementor on purpose."},{"line":679,"text":"- It must also name any test tiers left unrun, as `implement-change` requires."},{"line":680,"text":"- If the user wants the CLAUDE.md inspection requirement to apply after all, they need to say so. Until then this ruling stands."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-0c74b4fc9e9bc4f7 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":694,"end_line":706,"lines":[{"line":694,"text":"**Ruling:** Glyph-only detection does not satisfy the requirement. The spec names \"presentation chrome\" as an overlapping party in its own right, separate from \"visible text\"."},{"line":695,"text":"1. The helper must also collect the rectangle of each visible chrome element and test it against every other collected text or chrome rectangle."},{"line":696,"text":" - Chrome elements are the leaf chrome hooks outside the scene stage: `prev`, `next`, `progress-step`, `toc-entry`, `mode-toggle`, `attribution`, `caption`, `title`, `marker`, `document-title` and `brand`. A host-supplied attribution or brand counts too."},{"line":697,"text":" - Full-width structural containers (`header`, `footer`, `navigation`, `progress`, `toc`) are not collected. They span areas that scene content legitimately sits near and would make every step warn."},{"line":698,"text":"2. Skip any pair where one element is a DOM ancestor or descendant of the other, and any pair with the same owner. A button's own label inside the button is therefore not a collision."},{"line":699,"text":"3. Chrome inside an allow-overlap subtree stays exempt."},{"line":700,"text":"4. Scene non-text shapes (icons, boxes, arrows) are not a party unless they carry visible text. The requirement needs at least one text or chrome element on each side."},{"line":701,"text":"5. Warnings stay advisory and keep the `overlap: <a> / <b>` shape with readable chrome labels. The labels should name the hook or `aria-label`, plus the step as the helper already does."},{"line":702,"text":"6. Unit coverage should add a case for icon-only chrome overlapped by scene text. INT-002 should keep the unmarked-collision and allowed-overlap cases."},{"line":703,"text":""},{"line":704,"text":"**Rationale:** The literal wording lists chrome as an overlapping party. A button's padded box is part of that chrome and occupies the space viewers see. The shipped kit's own controls carry text, so glyph rectangles cover them partly, but the host-supplied attribution or brand and any restyled icon-only control show the gap. The alternative reading (glyph-only) is a plausible narrower interpretation, but it cannot be derived from the text. Emitting extra advisory warnings does not violate that reading, since the helper never fails a run on warnings (I-47)."},{"line":705,"text":""},{"line":706,"text":"**Pending from the user:** None blocking. Escalated for awareness only: if the user wants glyph-only detection as the deliberate scope, they must say so, because that would narrow the spec's \"text or presentation chrome\" wording."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-0c74b4fc9e9bc4f7 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":718,"end_line":730,"lines":[{"line":718,"text":"**Ruling:** An active control must be flagged when it is visually indistinguishable from any inactive control of the same kind, not only when identical to every inactive one, and not only to the first one found."},{"line":719,"text":"1. Compare the active control's computed visual signature against every inactive control of the same kind."},{"line":720,"text":"2. Emit one warning per active control. Keep the existing text, `indistinct active navigation: <kind> <label>`, so INT-002 and I-46 stay valid. Optionally append the matching peer label."},{"line":721,"text":"3. Add a unit case: inactive A distinct, inactive B identical to active C, which must warn."},{"line":722,"text":"4. Keep the uniform-inactive case warning, which it will under this ruling."},{"line":723,"text":""},{"line":724,"text":"**Rationale:**"},{"line":725,"text":"- The purpose is that a viewer can pick out the current step. If the current step looks the same as step B, they cannot tell the two apart, whatever step A looks like."},{"line":726,"text":"- The plural \"inactive controls\" in the requirement is a generic noun phrase, not a demand that the active state match every peer. Requiring a match with all of them would make the warning disappear in the common case of a disabled or visited neighbour."},{"line":727,"text":"- The existing `find` is an implementation shortcut with no support in the definition. The existing tests do not distinguish the two readings."},{"line":728,"text":"- Warnings are advisory, so the stricter reading does not conflict with the other one."},{"line":729,"text":""},{"line":730,"text":"**Pending from the user:** None blocking. Escalated for awareness: the \"match all inactive controls\" reading would yield fewer warnings. The user should override only if they want that."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-0c74b4fc9e9bc4f7 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":743,"end_line":764,"lines":[{"line":743,"text":"**Ruling:** The current behavior is compliant. Neither temporal resolution nor stroke drawing is mandated."},{"line":744,"text":"1. Row 7's scene intent is the end state of the step: a verify node chained after the cards, showing build and render checks with a green pass indicator. The verb \"resolve\" describes that state. A step in this model declares a state, and no intra-step checking sequence exists in the step model."},{"line":745,"text":"2. Row 9's scene intent is a labeled frame enclosing the whole existing diagram. \"Draws\" is the same loose verb the spec uses for connections, and it means the frame is added around retained entities. Motion timing and the style of entry (fade versus stroke) are deferred to design and not specified there."},{"line":746,"text":"3. A fading-in entry through the kit's normal newcomer behavior is acceptable and consistent with \"never rearranged or redrawn\"."},{"line":747,"text":"4. What the definition does require, and the implementation should keep:"},{"line":748,"text":" - The pass indication is visibly green."},{"line":749,"text":" - The frame's bounds enclose every retained entity."},{"line":750,"text":" - The frame carries its label."},{"line":751,"text":" - Earlier entities are not moved."},{"line":752,"text":"5. A real checking-to-pass transition or a drawn stroke would be allowed polish, not a requirement. Do not add either to satisfy the spec."},{"line":753,"text":"6. One watch item: the verify node's green is carried by its dark-green surface and light-green PASS text, with the check glyph near-white. A stricter reading of \"green pass check\" would want the check glyph itself green. That is a colour choice the definition leaves to design. It is not a compliance blocker, but the implementor may make the glyph green if cheap, with no change to the geometry."},{"line":754,"text":""},{"line":755,"text":"**Rationale:** The specification fixes steps, titles, captions and scene intent, and defers shape, layout, colour and motion timing. The checklist rows that verify these two beats ask only for resolved-state and added-frame assertions. Requiring animations the definition never describes would invent requirements."},{"line":756,"text":""},{"line":757,"text":"**Pending from the user:** None. Escalate only if the user intended \"resolve\" and \"draws\" as required animated sequences, which the definition does not state."},{"line":758,"text":""},{"line":759,"text":"## Summary: does any ruling block compliant implementation?"},{"line":760,"text":""},{"line":761,"text":"No ruling blocks implementation without a user decision."},{"line":762,"text":"- Q1 and Q2 have narrower alternate readings, glyph-only overlap and match-all inactive controls. The rulings take the broader readings, which the text supports. The only effect is more advisory warnings. They are recorded above as non-blocking escalations."},{"line":763,"text":"- Q3 requires no change."},{"line":764,"text":"- This pass was inspection-only. No tests, builds, product runs or repository edits were done."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-0c74b4fc9e9bc4f7 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":796,"end_line":821,"lines":[{"line":796,"text":"## Acceptance round 0, F-001: sample diagram text is 5 to 7 CSS pixels at a 390-pixel viewport"},{"line":797,"text":""},{"line":798,"text":"**Question:** At 390 × 844 the 880 × 380 canvas scales to about 0.389, so the card titles and labels render at roughly 5 to 7 CSS pixels. AT-003 expects \"important content remains readable ... at both viewport widths\". Should this be fixed?"},{"line":799,"text":""},{"line":800,"text":"**Requirement:**"},{"line":801,"text":"- `specs/evolving-scene-presentations/spec.md`, \"Fixed-canvas fit scaling\": the diagram is \"scaled uniformly to fit the available viewport, so the composition does not reflow\". \"The default design canvas SHALL be 880 × 380, with per-mode fit geometry for the browse and present layouts.\""},{"line":802,"text":"- Same file, \"Uniform scaling on resize\": scaling is uniform with no reflow of the internal composition."},{"line":803,"text":"- `design.md` Stage: scale is constant within a mode so `layoutId` morphs stay clean."},{"line":804,"text":"- `test-plan.md` AT-003 asks for readable content and a narrow-viewport pass."},{"line":805,"text":"- The sample's typography and geometry are deferred to design, and the sample must keep entities stationary across beats."},{"line":806,"text":""},{"line":807,"text":"**Ruling:** No code change, and I am escalating. The scale is determined by the approved fixed canvas: (390 − 2 × 24) / 880 = 0.389. Reaching comfortable text at that width needs one of:"},{"line":808,"text":"1. A different canvas or a narrow-viewport layout, which departs from the approved \"uniform scaling, no reflow\" requirement and the \"880 × 380 default\" requirement."},{"line":809,"text":"2. A per-viewport sample layout, which breaks the \"entities are never rearranged\" sample requirement unless a second composition is authored."},{"line":810,"text":"3. Larger sample typography on the existing geometry. That is within the presentation's own design latitude, but the cards are 132 × 86 and the smallest labels are already 9 to 12 px. Even 16 px design text renders at about 6 px, so it cannot meet a comfortable reading size, and I cannot confirm in this step that larger text would fit the cards without new collisions."},{"line":811,"text":""},{"line":812,"text":"I did not change the margin or typography. The change would be marginal (the margin saves a few percent of scale) and cannot reach comfortable readability, and it adds unverified risk."},{"line":813,"text":""},{"line":814,"text":"**Rationale:** The observation is correct, but it follows from approved requirements. The narrow-view expectation in AT-003 and the fixed-canvas requirement can only both hold if \"readable\" is read as \"legible when zoomed or as part of a scaled whole\", which is a product decision."},{"line":815,"text":""},{"line":816,"text":"**Pending from the user (decision needed):** Choose one:"},{"line":817,"text":"- (a) Accept the uniform-scale behavior at phone widths as intended. AT-003's narrow-view clause is then interpreted as \"fits without reflow or collision\"."},{"line":818,"text":"- (b) Approve a narrow-viewport mechanism (a second per-mode canvas, a minimum scale with scrolling, or an authored narrow composition). That changes the fixed-canvas and no-reflow requirements and needs a spec update."},{"line":819,"text":"- (c) Approve modest typography increases in the sample only, accepting that this will not reach comfortable readability at 390 px."},{"line":820,"text":""},{"line":821,"text":"Until the user decides, the implementation stays as is."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-0c74b4fc9e9bc4f7 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":849,"end_line":859,"lines":[{"line":849,"text":"## Acceptance round 1, F-001: carried over, still awaiting the user"},{"line":850,"text":""},{"line":851,"text":"**Question:** The tester reproduced the 5 to 7 px diagram text at 390 × 844 again (scale 0.389)."},{"line":852,"text":""},{"line":853,"text":"**Requirement:** Unchanged from the \"Acceptance round 0, F-001\" entry above: fixed 880 × 380 canvas, uniform scaling, no internal reflow, and AT-003's narrow-view readability expectation."},{"line":854,"text":""},{"line":855,"text":"**Ruling:** No code change this round. The behavior still follows from the approved fixed-canvas requirement, and the choice between (a) accepting it, (b) approving a narrow-viewport mechanism with a spec update, or (c) modest sample typography increases is the user's decision, as recorded in the round 0 entry and in \"Narrow viewport readability threshold\"."},{"line":856,"text":""},{"line":857,"text":"**Rationale:** Any fix changes the approved scaling or sample composition requirements. Nothing new was learned that changes that assessment."},{"line":858,"text":""},{"line":859,"text":"**Pending from the user (decision needed):** Choose (a), (b) or (c) as described in the round 0 F-001 entry."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-0c74b4fc9e9bc4f7 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":866,"end_line":868,"lines":[{"line":866,"text":"## Decision brief"},{"line":867,"text":""},{"line":868,"text":"The current fix restores overlap diagnostics for text-bearing chrome with a visible background or border while preserving glyph-only handling for undecorated full-width text. F-002 and F-003 now pass their retests. F-001, the small diagram labels at a narrow viewport, still reproduces and remains unresolved. Decision: NOT READY. Suggested review path: review F-001 and the narrow-readability decision in the assumptions ledger; then retest after any resulting product or specification change."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-1754e2bee5a73ca0 (final-handoff)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":1008,"end_line":1012,"lines":[{"line":1008,"text":"### Step E1 — Materialization process boundary and caller CWD"},{"line":1009,"text":""},{"line":1010,"text":"- **Prediction from approved behavior:** Invoking the bundled helper by absolute path from a CWD outside the skill will materialize the same bootstrap anchors; its package will install/build in isolation and the sample route will pass browser verification."},{"line":1011,"text":"- **Observation:** Helper copied files from the skill-relative template into an empty scratch target when called from the scratch CWD. `npm ci --offline` installed 243 packages; `npm run build`, bootstrap `npm run verify`, and bootstrap `npm run inspect -- example` all exited 0. It covers a background, a border, and a fully transparent background (no box)."},{"line":841,"text":"- `evidence/F-003-unit.log` shows 11 of 11 passing. `evidence/F-003-unit-prefix.log` shows the new case failing against the previous script."},{"line":842,"text":"- `evidence/F-003-lint.log` and `evidence/F-003-types.log` are clean."},{"line":843,"text":"- The root script and the bootstrap template copy are byte-identical."},{"line":844,"text":""},{"line":845,"text":"**Integration regression recommendation:** INT-002 should add a styled-brand fixture whose box overlaps scene text and a plain full-width marker next to a right-aligned button, asserting a warning for the first and none for the second in real browser geometry. Not added now because integration suites are not run in this step."},{"line":846,"text":""},{"line":847,"text":"**Pending from the user:** None."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-0c74b4fc9e9bc4f7 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":38,"end_line":38,"lines":[{"line":38,"text":" \"text\": \"## ADDED Requirements\\n\\n### Requirement: Interactive requirement gathering\\nThe skill SHALL gather presentation details by asking the user clarifying questions one at a time — covering the topic, the visual style, and the content and visual description of each step. The user controls how much to specify; the skill SHALL NOT assume details the user can still provide, but SHALL allow the user to proceed with partial detail and iterate. The skill MAY, at its discretion, draw ASCII mockups to represent key or complex steps when doing so helps confirm the intended visual layout.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Prompt is missing details\\n- **WHEN** the skill is invoked with a prompt that omits the topic, visual style, or per-step descriptions\\n- **THEN** the skill asks for the missing information one question at a time rather than assuming it\\n\\n#### Scenario: User proceeds with partial detail\\n- **WHEN** the user chooses to build after providing only some details\\n- **THEN** the skill generates a presentation from what was captured without blocking on a hard completeness gate\\n\\n#### Scenario: Prompt already complete\\n- **WHEN** the prompt already contains the topic, style, and all step details\\n- **THEN** the skill may proceed to build without further questions\\n\\n#### Scenario: ASCII mockup for a complex step\\n- **WHEN** a step's visual layout is key or complex\\n- **THEN** the skill may present an ASCII mockup of that step to the user to confirm the layout before building, without doing so for every step\\n\\n### Requirement: Self-bootstrapping scaffold\\nBefore creating or modifying a presentation, the skill SHALL ensure the project provides the infrastructure a generated presentation depends on, SHALL resolve where that infrastructure belongs, and SHALL scaffold whatever is missing — including installing the dependencies the infrastructure requires. The required infrastructure is three contract anchors:\\n\\n1. **Build setup** — a Vite + React + TypeScript app with a working `npm run build`.\\n2. **Scene kit** — the reusable, presentation-agnostic engine: the `Step`/`Scene` step contract, the stage/host that mounts the active step and runs entity morphs, the present/browse navigation, and the chrome (captions, table of contents) and fit-scale canvas.\\n3. **Presentation index** — the registry that maps each presentation to its own route so that multiple presentations coexist.\\n\\nDetection is contract-level, keyed on the presence of these anchors rather than a byte-identical scaffold, so cosmetic differences (file naming, formatting, extra dependencies) do not trigger re-scaffolding. When scaffolding, the skill SHALL NOT assume the required dependencies are already installed.\\n\\nThe scaffold SHALL be styling-framework-neutral and SHALL ship with zero presentation styling defaults. It SHALL install the runtime and build dependencies needed for React, Vite, TypeScript, Motion, Lucide icons, linting, and render verification, but it SHALL NOT require Tailwind, a Tailwind Vite plugin, a default CSS theme, default colors, default fonts, default card styles, default button styles, or any other styling framework. Styling systems MAY be added by the presentation author or host project after scaffolding.\\n\\nThe skill SHALL resolve scaffold templates relative to the skill file that declares them, so agents do not depend on the user's current working directory when locating `templates/bootstrap/` or presentation templates.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Empty or fully unscaffolded directory\\n- **WHEN** the skill runs in an empty directory or a project with none of the three anchors present\\n- **THEN** it performs a full scaffold (build setup, scene kit, and presentation index) and installs the required dependencies before creating the presentation\\n\\n#### Scenario: Already scaffolded\\n- **WHEN** all three anchors are already present\\n- **THEN** the skill skips scaffolding and proceeds directly to creating or modifying the presentation\\n\\n#### Scenario: Partial scaffold\\n- **WHEN** some but not all anchors are present\\n- **THEN** the skill scaffolds only the missing anchors (and their dependencies) without disturbing the ones already present\\n\\n#### Scenario: Scaffold does not impose a style system\\n- **WHEN** the skill scaffolds a presentation app\\n- **THEN** the generated app can build without Tailwind or another styling framework\\n- **AND** the scaffold does not define default presentation colors, fonts, spacing scale, card styles, button styles, borders, shadows, or CSS theme tokens\\n\\n#### Scenario: Templates resolve from skill directory\\n- **WHEN** the skill copies bootstrap or presentation templates\\n- **THEN** it resolves those paths relative to the skill's own `SKILL.md` directory\\n\\n#### Scenario: Monorepo target\\n- **WHEN** the skill runs inside a monorepo\\n- **THEN** it scaffolds the presentation app into a `presentations/` directory as its own self-contained app rather than at the repository root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Standalone project target\\n- **WHEN** the skill scaffolds in an empty or standalone (non-monorepo) project\\n- **THEN** it scaffolds the presentation app at the repository root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Non-empty project missing scaffolding\\n- **WHEN** the project is non-empty but lacks the scene kit or presentation index\\n- **THEN** the skill states the target location it will scaffold into and proceeds only after the user confirms\\n\\n### Requirement: Create a new presentation\\nThe skill SHALL generate a new presentation as a self-contained unit reachable at its own route and registered so that multiple presentations coexist.\\n\\n#### Scenario: New presentation is self-contained and routed\\n- **WHEN** a new presentation is created\\n- **THEN** it is written as its own folder, reachable at its own route, and registered in the presentation index\\n\\n#### Scenario: Presentation owns its visual style\\n- **WHEN** the skill creates a presentation with a designed visual look\\n- **THEN** the styling is added in files owned by that presentation or by the host app rather than in the reusable scene kit\\n- **AND** plain CSS is the default styling approach unless the host project already uses a styling framework or the user explicitly requests one\\n\\n#### Scenario: Existing presentations are preserved\\n- **WHEN** a new presentation is created and other presentations already exist\\n- **THEN** the existing presentations remain intact and reachable\\n\\n### Requirement: Modify an existing presentation\\nThe skill SHALL support modifying an existing presentation, identifying the target first and asking only about the requested changes.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Target unspecified or ambiguous\\n- **WHEN** the skill is asked to modify a presentation without a clear target\\n- **THEN** it lists the existing presentations and asks which to modify before changing anything\\n\\n#### Scenario: Scoped modification\\n- **WHEN** the target presentation is identified\\n- **THEN** the skill asks only about the requested changes (steps, entities, or style) and edits that presentation without re-walking the full create flow\\n\\n### Requirement: Self-verify before reporting completion\\nBefore reporting success, the skill SHALL confirm that the generated or modified presentation builds, renders without errors, and is visually coherent in a browser, fixing any failures itself. The render check SHALL at minimum render the presentation's first step without runtime or console errors; the full multi-step render check across every step is defined by the `presentation-verification` capability. The visual composition check SHALL inspect screenshots or an equivalent browser view of the first step, the last step, and any dense/key steps; responsive-sensitive presentations SHALL also be checked at a narrow viewport. When a project-local screenshot helper is available, the skill SHALL prefer it over ad hoc scripts outside the project tree so browser tooling resolves from local dependencies, settled screenshots are captured after animations complete, and advisory visual warnings can be reviewed.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Checks run before done\\n- **WHEN** the skill finishes generating or modifying a presentation\\n- **THEN** it runs the build, at least a first-step render check, and a browser visual composition check before reporting completion\\n\\n#### Scenario: Failures are fixed, not reported as success\\n- **WHEN** the build, render, or visual composition check fails\\n- **THEN** the skill fixes the issues and re-checks rather than reporting success\\n\\n### Requirement: Generated presentation quality bar\\nEvery generated presentation SHALL build with no type errors, render its first step without runtime errors, present a caption per step, support next/previous navigation, pass a visual composition check, and conform to the evolving-scene model.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Builds clean\\n- **WHEN** a presentation is generated\\n- **THEN** `npm run build` completes with no type errors\\n\\n#### Scenario: Renders without errors\\n- **WHEN** the presentation route is opened\\n- **THEN** it renders its first step with no runtime or console errors\\n\\n#### Scenario: Captions and navigation present\\n- **WHEN** viewing a presentation\\n- **THEN** each step shows a caption and the user can navigate to the next and previous steps\\n\\n#### Scenario: Visual composition is inspected\\n- **WHEN** a presentation is generated or modified\\n- **THEN** key browser screenshots or equivalent browser views show that important scene content fits the fixed canvas, intentional overlaps remain readable, and content does not collide with chrome such as captions, progress indicators, table of contents, or navigation controls\\n\\n#### Scenario: Screenshot helper is project-local\\n- **WHEN** the skill captures screenshots for visual inspection\\n- **THEN** it uses the scaffolded project-local helper when available, or otherwise writes any temporary Playwright helper under the project root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Visual warnings are reviewed\\n- **WHEN** the screenshot helper emits overlap or chrome-polish warnings\\n- **THEN** the skill reviews the referenced steps, fixes accidental collisions or indistinct current-step chrome, and marks only intentional readable overlaps as allowed\\n\\n#### Scenario: Active chrome and attribution are styled locally\\n- **WHEN** the generated presentation includes table-of-contents, progress, navigation, or attribution chrome\\n- **THEN** presentation-owned or host-owned CSS makes the active step visibly distinct and the attribution legible\\n- **AND** the reusable scene kit remains free of default colors, fonts, borders, button styles, and theme tokens\\n\""}],"label":"[harness frame or verified index]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":1008,"end_line":1012,"lines":[{"line":1008,"text":"### Step E1 — Materialization process boundary and caller The rubric fails a skill only in two cases: it tells the agent to report completion without defining what the report contains, or its report template leaves out a required item. SKILL.md&#39;s closing paragraph does define the contents. It names the route, the changed files, the build and render checks, the visual views reviewed and any remaining advisory warnings, and it says to report them &#39;accurately&#39;, which means reporting outcomes and not just listing items. Section 4 describes `npm run inspect -- &lt;slug&gt;` as the tool that captures every step and prints advisory diagnostics. Read with that section, &#39;visual views reviewed&#39; (the captures) and &#39;remaining advisory warnings&#39; (the diagnostics) together cover the inspect results. The original fail depends on two things the requirement does not demand: the literal word &#39;inspect&#39; and a formatted template. The required items are each named, so the requirement is met.","evidence":["SKILL.md final paragraph: &#39;Report the route, changed files, build/render checks, visual views reviewed, and any remaining advisory warnings accurately. The deck numbers its steps from 0 (`data-step-index` starts at 0, and inspect loops from `index = 0` to `count - 1`), so step 0 is simply the first step. Rejecting it would make the first step impossible to capture. Read this way, the helper does what the requirement asks. readStepCount throws when the count is not an integer or is below 1, which covers missing, zero and non-numeric counts. settleStep waits for `data-step-index` to equal `String(index)` exactly and throws after its 3000 ms timeout otherwise, so a missing, non-numeric or wrong index stops the run before any capture.
